title: Portfolio Overlap
blurb: When more funds means the same portfolio: measuring overlap, reading the bands, and consolidating with care.

rows: New employees (all sections), sales team (talk-tracks, role-plays, niche topics); investors as awareness material
About 75 minutes of lessons, plus role-play and the final quiz
Each L.E.A.R.N. stage has: what to know, how to do it, a talk-track, and the investor takeaway

sources: SEBI Master Circular for Mutual Funds (current edition)
SEBI circular on categorisation and rationalisation of schemes (26 February 2026)

questions.q: What is portfolio overlap?
o: The share of one fund’s holdings also held by another
A fund’s return over the index
questions.why: The share of one fund’s holdings also held by another. High overlap means two funds act like one.

questions.q: How is overlap between two funds usually calculated?
o: Add the larger weights of shared stocks
Add the smaller weights of shared stocks
questions.why: Add the smaller weights of shared stocks. Sum of the smaller weight for each common stock.

questions.q: Shared stocks at 8%, 6%, 6%, 4% (smaller weights) give overlap of…
SEBI defines large-cap companies as…
questions.why: Top 100 by market capitalisation. Per AMFI’s half-yearly list.

questions.q: Large-cap funds must hold at least…
questions.why: 80% in large caps. Which is why they overlap heavily.

questions.q: Under SEBI’s February 2026 circular, an AMC’s value and contra funds may overlap by no more than…
questions.why: 50%. Both can be offered only within this limit.

questions.q: The 50% overlap cap with other equity schemes applies to…
questions.why: Sectoral and thematic schemes. Large-cap schemes are excepted from the comparison.

questions.q: Do SEBI’s overlap limits prevent overlap across different AMCs?
o: No, they apply within one AMC
questions.why: No, they apply within one AMC. We still need to check the client’s portfolio.

questions.q: In our teaching guide, overlap above 50% between two funds suggests…
questions.why: Consider keeping one of them. They are largely the same portfolio.

questions.q: What is the cheapest first step when consolidating?
o: Stop new money into funds being dropped and redirect it
questions.why: Stop new money into funds being dropped and redirect it. Costs nothing.

questions.q: In core and satellite, the core is usually…
o: 1–2 broad funds like flexi-cap or index
questions.why: 1–2 broad funds like flexi-cap or index. About 60–80% of equity, illustratively.

questions.q: Which is a sign of a cluttered portfolio?
o: Three large-cap funds from different AMCs
questions.why: Three large-cap funds from different AMCs. Same category, same stocks.

questions.q: A client holds ESOPs in his employer, which his funds also hold. You should…
o: Count the direct holding when assessing concentration
Buy more of the employer’s stock
questions.why: Count the direct holding when assessing concentration. Direct holdings add to overlap and concentration.

questions.q: “Different AMCs are safer” is answered by…
o: “Scheme assets sit with a trust and custodian; what matters is what funds own”
questions.why: “Scheme assets sit with a trust and custodian; what matters is what funds own”. Diversify holdings, not fund houses.

questions.q: Which statement is compliant?
o: “Let’s check overlap, costs and your goals, then decide which funds to keep, with your approval.”
questions.why: “Let’s check overlap, costs and your goals, then decide which funds to keep, with your approval.”. Base changes on goals, risk and costs; record approval.

questions.q: Does owning more funds always mean more diversification?
o: No — funds often hold the same top stocks
Yes, if they are from different AMCs
questions.why: Funds often hold the same top stocks.

questions.q: How is overlap between two funds usually calculated?
o: Add the larger weights of shared stocks
Add the smaller weight of each shared stock
questions.why: Add the smaller weights of shared stocks. Sum of the smaller weight for each common stock.

questions.q: Do SEBI's 2026 overlap limits apply across all AMCs a client uses?
o: No, they apply within one fund house
questions.why: They apply within one AMC. We still need to check the client's portfolio.

questions.q: What is the cheapest first step when consolidating?
o: Stop new money into funds being dropped and redirect it
questions.why: Stop new money into funds being dropped and redirect it. Costs nothing.

questions.q: Should a fund be added once it is top-rated, without checking overlap?
o: No — always check what it adds to existing holdings
Only if it is a small-cap fund
questions.why: Always check what it adds to existing holdings.

questions.q: Suresh has 14 equity funds with ₹1,000 SIPs each. What do you propose?
o: Check overlap; propose a core-satellite structure of 4–5 funds; redirect SIPs first; check exit loads and tax before any redemption; record his approval
questions.why: Check overlap; propose a core-satellite structure of 4–5 funds; redirect SIPs first; check exit loads and tax before any redemption; record his approval.

questions.q: Divya holds three large-cap funds from different AMCs “for safety”. What do you explain?
o: Agree — different AMCs are always safer
Show their high overlap; explain safety comes from what is owned, not the number of AMCs; suggest keeping one core fund
Switch everything to a single AMC for safety
questions.why: Show their high overlap; explain safety comes from what is owned, not the number of AMCs; suggest keeping one core fund.

questions.q: A client wants to add last year's top flexi-cap fund. What do you do first?
o: Check its overlap with existing funds; ask what job it would do; add only if it brings something different
Replace all existing funds with it
Ignore overlap and follow the rating
questions.why: Check its overlap with existing funds; ask what job it would do; add only if it brings something different.

questions.q: Kiran holds many employer shares via ESOPs, and his funds also hold that stock. What do you do?
o: Count the direct holding; review sector and stock concentration; consider funds with less exposure to that sector
Buy more of the employer's stock
questions.why: Count the direct holding; review sector and stock concentration; consider funds with less exposure to that sector.

questions.q: A client receives a notice that a thematic fund is being merged. How do you respond?
o: Explain SEBI's overlap rules as the likely reason; review the merged scheme's portfolio, risk and costs; explain the exit option
questions.why: Explain SEBI's overlap rules as the likely reason; review the merged scheme's portfolio, risk and costs; explain the exit option.
